scientific_limitations_integrity: The theorem concerns finite-dimensional systems at positive temperature and finite uniform field, with a field coupled to an additive charge exactly conserved by the zero-field Hamiltonian. It proves invariance of partial-transpose inertia, not invariance of negativity magnitude, separability in dimensions above 2x3, or behavior under transverse/nonuniform fields. Field-independent threshold behavior is explicitly prior for selected spin-one parameters and for an own-ledger pure-biquadratic special case; originality is limited to the general Gibbs-to-local-filter congruence, the resulting all-parameter full-inertia theorem, and its consequence that every partial-transpose zero-crossing temperature is field independent. The proof is analytic and the packaged exact checker only replays its finite spin-one algebraic ingredients.
title: Uniform longitudinal fields preserve partial-transpose inertia in charge-conserving thermal dimers
